Title: The calendar and the player registry are back online

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Fellow players,

The VEKN modules had been unavailable since the site was upgraded to the latest version after the attacks that crashed the servers a few months ago.

As a consequence, the VEKN modules weren't compatible any more, and it's been a tedious task upgrading them.

Now that they are available again, I strongly recommand that everyone checks that the events that took place since the crash are created and the results entered. This is important for some players that care for ranking, but also to have a list of qualified players up to date.

If you played an event that is not registered, please contact your local prince or the organizer of the event to have the results entered. I'm counting on everyone as I didn't receive all the results, and I rely on the organizers to have the job being done.

Thanks, and enjoy!

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
People get added to the registry when the participate to a tournament. The tournament organizer (usually a Prince) has access to the Prince forum and can ask for new VEKN ids to be created.

In addition to what Ankha said:

VEKN FAQ: www.vekn.net/v-ekn-faq

2.8. How do I assign a V:EKN number to a new player?

Search the Player Registry for V:EKN numbers starting with your Prince prefix, sort them by "V:EKN ID#" and then choose the next V:EKN number available.

2.9. How do I add a new player to the Player Registry?

Contact the Website Coordinator and send him the following information:
1) Player's first name(s):
2) Player's last name(s):
3) City:
4) State/province (optional):
5) Country:
6) E-mail address (optional):
7) V:EKN ID# provided by his or her Prince (which is the general Prince prefix followed by 4 digits):
Volunteers can check V:EKN numbers availability in the Player Registry.

V:EKN Website Coordinator
